newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - July 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - July 29.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on July 29. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

The Tirtamas group headed by Hashim Djojohadikusumo has reached an agreement with the majority shareholder in Bank Niaga for their 40 percent share in the bank as well as put out a tender offer for a further 10 percent.

The chaotic condition caused by the arrival of thousands of soccer hooligans from East Java over the last few days has forced the government to think about the possibility of moving the venue of the national soccer league finals from Jakarta to other cities.
President Suharto said the Indonesian armed forces (ABRI) should implement its dual function doctrine, which justifies its involvement in socio-political affairs, with care and alertness.

A visiting American academic, Professor Jeffrey Winters, has criticised the World Bank for not taking the necessary action to lessen around 30 percent loan leakage in Indonesia, which is considered its "model" debtor country.
